ImageDescription.value: Built between 1960-64, the Confederation Centre of the Arts is an arts centre containing a theatre, an art gallery, and a library.  Although the Confederation Centre of the Arts was built as a national memorial to the Fathers of Confederation who met at the Charlottetown Conference, the Centre is not itself dedicated to the Conference or to Confederation in general.  Instead, the art gallery has a permanent collection of Canadian art and also has exhibit space for traveling shows, while the theatre hosts traveling Broadway musicals and the annual "Anne of Green Gables - The Musical."

ImageDescription.value: The full name of the Ropeway of Darjeeling is Ranjit Valley Passenger Ropeway. It is one of the India's oldest passenger ropeways and connects Darjeeling to Shingla Bazaar. It starts from North point, accommodating six passengers at a time. In its travel the cabin sways above green tea gardens, dense forest, streams and green valley with the view of the Mount Kanchenjunga along its way. This first bi-cable ropeway is the longest of its kind in Asia, and is 4620 mt. long.

ImageDescription.value:
Keventer's restaurant exterior view at Darjeeling town. It is a heritage restaurant.

In 1911 Mr. Edwards Keventers set up a cozy corner restaurant in this small hill station offering, not just milk products, but it boasted a classic English Breakfast with exclusive premium Darjeeling Tea, making it a must-go for the elites who came to Darjeeling.

At present the restaurant has been owned by the Jha family. For three generations now, the family has served and preserved the culture of the restaurant and thrived further.

ImageDescription.value:
Bhutia Busty monastery or Karma Dorjee Chyoling monastery is a Buddhist monastery located in Bhutia Busty, Darjeeling District India. It belongs to the Red Sect of Buddhist Lamas.
The origin of name Darjeeling is linked to this monastery 'Dorjee', means thunderbolt in Tibetan and 'Ling' means resting place, thus 'Place' of the 'Thunderbolt' which was the name of the Monastery, originally located on the Observatory Hill before it was sacked by the Nepalese in the 19th century and rebuilt on the present site. The ill-fated Monastery was destroyed by the 1934 earthquake and owes its present existence to the munificence of the Late Raja of Sikkim.

ImageDescription.value:
Samten Choeling Monastery at Ghoom in Darjeeling district.
This  Monastery belongs to the Gelukpa sect of Vajrayana Buddhism, also known as the yellow hat. This is the seat of ven. Dromo Geshe rinpoche, the second. The monastery has a rich collection of rare books on Buddhism. Situated at an altitude of 8,000 feet from sea level, the Ghoom monastery (also known as Samten Choling monastery), is one of the better known monasteries of Darjeeling. Said to have been built in mid 19th century by Lama Sherab Gyatso, it is famous for its 15 feet tall statue of Maitreya Buddha (future Buddha).
